rationale: Aripiprazole (partial D2/D3 agonist, very long half-life ~75 h plus dehydroaripiprazole ~94 h) to amisulpride (full D2 antagonist). Common reasons: insufficient positive symptom control on aripiprazole, need for more sedation, or intolerable akathisia from aripiprazole. Because aripiprazole's half-life is extremely long, effective plasma levels persist for 3–5 weeks after the last dose. This means that amisulpride can be started at full therapeutic dose from day 1 — aripiprazole's residual partial agonism provides a natural buffer against abrupt coverage loss. The cross-taper can be shorter than usual for this reason. ECG required: amisulpride prolongs QTc; baseline before starting. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

schedule.notes: Start amisulpride 400 mg at full therapeutic dose. Continue aripiprazole 15 mg. Aripiprazole's very long half-life (active drug persists 3–5 weeks after stopping) means full D2 coverage is maintained throughout. Baseline ECG for amisulpride.
Plateau both drugs. Amisulpride approaching steady state. QTc: check baseline ECG if not done. Aripiprazole plasma levels are still present despite any dose reduction.
Reduce aripiprazole to 10 mg. Amisulpride well established. Expect resolution of aripiprazole-associated akathisia or insomnia if these were the reason for switching.
Reduce aripiprazole to 5 mg. Effective aripiprazole levels remain clinically significant due to the long half-life even at this low dose.
Stop aripiprazole. Continue amisulpride 400 mg. Note: residual aripiprazole will continue to wash out for several further weeks — EPS and QTc picture stabilises gradually. Repeat ECG at 6 weeks.

doseRatios.equivalencyNote: Aripiprazole 15 mg ≈ amisulpride 400 mg (Leucht et al. CMD method, Schizophrenia Bulletin 2015). PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.
